text:
Zoe Miller: Hi team — first day. Followed the onboarding steps but when I tried to create my dev namespace I got `already exists`. I expected lena-dev but it shows lena-dev owned by another user? Who owns namespaces so we can avoid collisions?

Alex Turner: welcome Zoe :wave: Namespaces are global per-cluster. Sounds like someone created a similarly named namespace earlier (maybe a stale onboarding namespace). Can you paste `kubectl get namespace lena-dev -o yaml` (sanitized)?

Zoe Miller: sanitized output shows metadata.ownerReferences absent but annotation `created-by: onboarding-bot` and `created-for: lena@redwood.ai`. So it's lena's namespace. I was trying `lena-dev` as a convention but assumed unique per user.

Priya Sharma: quick note — we prefer the pattern `<firstname>-dev-<shortid>` to avoid collisions, e.g., `zoe-dev-14`. For new hires we create namespaces on request; if you want a specific name we can check availability or transfer ownership.

Alex Turner: @onboard-bot can we check if `lena-dev` is active or stale? If stale we can reclaim after confirming with owner.

onboard-bot: Namespace check: `lena-dev` last active 2026-09-02T14:03:21Z; owner annotation lena@redwood.ai. No reclamation flagged.

Zoe Miller: ok I'll pick `zoe-dev-14` then. Could you create `zoe-dev-14` and grant edit? Need to port-forward for previews.

Alex Turner: creating namespace `zoe-dev-14` and RoleBinding `rb-zoe-dev-14-edit` to `okta:zoe@redwood.ai` now.

Alex Turner: done — give it a few seconds and try `kubectl get pods -n zoe-dev-14`.

Zoe Miller: `kubectl get pods -n zoe-dev-14` -> no resources found. Set default namespace and port-forward works. Thanks!

Priya Sharma: added a short note to onboarding doc about collision-safe namespace naming and to ping #devex when you want a specific name reserved. Welcome aboard!
